note: Requirements collected from the owner's brief (2026-11-06) and organized by category. Technical requirements are backed by manufacturer/industry sources; owner-stated requirements are labeled USER-BRIEF.

requirements.requirement: Remove and/or replace the bathtub wastewater overflow trip lever (the stuck lever is inside the hidden plumbing behind the wall) and restore stopper open/close function.
If the plunger/linkage can be freed by repair or adjustment (rather than full replacement), that lower-impact fix is acceptable; one estimate covers adjust/repair only ($135, EST-3).
Removal from above (through the overflow plate) is the preferred method if it can be done safely.
requirements.source: USER-BRIEF (2026-11-06); standard above-removal procedure S6, S7

requirements.requirement: 5+ licensed plumbers have already been unable to remove the assembly from above without concern over destroying the hidden plumbing behind the wall; forceful above-removal is excluded (documented risk of breaking the plunger rod off inside the piping).

Fallback: work from below. The waste-and-overflow working joints (drain shoe, tee, overflow elbow) are reached from below/behind the tub; this may require opening the drywall ceiling (a storage unit is directly below).
requirements.source: USER-BRIEF (2026-11-06) + assembly location S1, S4; access-from-below practice S9, S10

requirements.requirement: All-in-one service: the hired outfit must cover plumbing AND drywall/ceiling patch, texture and paint (single point of contact; drywall repair is a separate trade/cost in industry guidance).
requirements.source: USER-BRIEF (2026-11-06) + S8 (drywall access raises cost; plumbers may bring a separate contractor), S9 (drywall/ceiling repair is a separate cost)

requirements.requirement: Provider must be a licensed plumber or licensed contractor (verify license on the official CSLB lookup before hiring).
requirements.source: USER-BRIEF (2026-11-06) + S11 (CSLB Check a License), S12 (SF DBI directs owners to licensed professionals)

requirements.requirement: Provider must service the San Francisco location of the unit.

Tenants occupy the unit where the trip lever is stuck. Work must be performed as delicate work in a sensitive, occupied environment: dust/debris containment, water shutoff coordination, cleanup, and reasonable scheduling.
A storage unit lies directly below the bathtub; any ceiling opening must be planned around stored contents, and the ceiling must be closed and finished after the plumbing work.

Every entry published on this site carries a source link to an official site. Values that cannot be confirmed from an official source are left blank and flagged UNVERIFIED. No value is ever inferred or filled in.

Before hiring: confirm CSLB license status, ask for a written itemized quote that separates plumbing scope from drywall/finish scope, and confirm the provider has executed below-access waste-and-overflow work in occupied units.
